context.context: The Costa Concordia disaster occurred on January 13, 2012, when the cruise ship, operated by Costa Crociere, struck a rock off the coast of Isola del Giglio, resulting in the capsizing of the ship and loss of 32 lives. The refloating operation, which is the subject of this image, represents a significant step in the long-term recovery and salvage process of the vessel. The operation involves complex engineering techniques to safely raise the ship from the seabed and remove it from the site, a process that might take weeks, if not months, to complete. This image captures the moment when workers are setting out to begin this critical operation, reflecting the culmination of years of planning and efforts to address the aftermath of one of the worst maritime disasters in recent history.
